verses.1: For the choirmaster. A psalm of David. To be remembered.
verses.2: God, come to my aid. LORD, hasten to help me.
verses.3: Let those who seek my life be put to shame and be humiliated. Let those who long for my downfall be turned back and be disgraced.
verses.4: Let those who say to me, “Aha! Aha!” be turned back and be ashamed.
verses.5: Let all who seek you rejoice and be glad in you. Let them always say, “The LORD is great!” May lovers of your salvation say continually, “The LORD is great!”
verses.6: But I am poor and in need. LORD, be my helper. You are my aid and my deliverer. LORD, do not delay.

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: "To be remembered" (לְהַזְכִּֽיר) is an interpretive rendering of the word typically translated as "for remembrance" or "as a memorial." Here, it reflects the idea that this psalm should be recalled or preserved.
- v. 4: The phrase "Aha! Aha!" (הֶאָח הֶאָח) is a common expression of triumph in Hebrew literature, often used by enemies of the righteous. It is retained in direct form to preserve the tone.
